title: Cancelable progress & escape semantics for primary/icon buttons across themes
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Define and deliver a consistent cancelable progress pattern for primary and icon-only buttons. The goal is to make long-running button actions visibly cancellable, keyboard-escape friendly, and theme-adaptive without regressing existing token contracts or hit-target behaviour.
background: We continue to see frontend and product teams adding bespoke loading/error cancel flows when a user needs to abort an in-flight action (e.g., large file upload, model eval, or expensive rerank). Current button loading states are opaque in some themes (spinner-only) and do not expose a reliable escape/cancel affordance for keyboard users or when theme contrast is low. Engineering has requested a single design spec so their implementation can be reused across Console, Deploy flows, and the QuickStart templates.
goals: Provide a clear, accessible cancel affordance for primary and icon buttons during long-running actions
Standardize keyboard escape (Esc) behavior to cancel actions and restore focus semantics
Keep token surface stable: avoid introducing extra tokens where token churn would break older releases
Ensure visual parity across light, dark, and high-contrast themes and at three density scales
non_goals: Creating new button APIs beyond a simple 'cancelable' prop mapping
acceptance_criteria: Design specs for primary, secondary, and icon-only buttons with cancelable progress in Figma
Prototype (React) demonstrating ESC-to-cancel + visible progress fallback for low-contrast themes
Accessibility checklist validated: ARIA-live region for progress updates, proper aria-busy, and keyboard focus preserved after cancel
Token usage documented and no breaking token renames introduced
UX sign-off from PM (Arjun Patel) and a11y review by Simone Lee
tasks: Audit existing button usage in Console and QuickStart to find components that need cancellation support
Create Figma frames: primary-cancelable / icon-cancelable / compact variants in all theme tokens
Document expected keyboard semantics (Esc behavior, focus return) and a11y roles
Share PR checklist for eng: props, events (onCancel), aria attributes, and token mapping
Collect implementation feedback from ENG Buttons owners and iterate
comments: 2025-02-11 - Maya Thompson: Initial write-up and goals posted. Noted that previous spinner-only pattern fails WCAG 2.1 contrast tests in low-contrast theme; requested a fallback text label.
2025-02-12 - Luca Ramirez: Rough Figma concepts uploaded. Two approaches: overlay cancel icon vs replace label with 'Cancel'. Leaning toward replace label for primary to reduce hit-target shift.
2025-02-14 - Simone Lee (a11y): Asked to ensure ESC triggers both onCancel callback and an ARIA announcement. Also requested examples with screen-reader VO/JA toggles in the prototype.
2025-02-16 - Arjun Patel (PM): Prioritize primary and icon-only variants for Console flows; QuickStart can adopt later. Agreed to keep token changes minimal.
2025-02-18 - Luca Ramirez: Updated prototype added to PR #782. Waiting on ENG-4321 for final onCancel wiring. Filed follow-up ENG task for backend abort hook.
decisions: Use text-replacement pattern for primary buttons during cancelable actions (e.g., 'Saving…' -> 'Cancel') to avoid adding nested controls
Icon-only buttons will show a transient 'x' overlay in center for a short duration, then fall back to spinner if cancel is not acted on
ESC key will trigger onCancel event, update aria-live region with cancellation message, and return focus to the original control
No new tokens will be introduced; reuse existing semantic tokens and document mapping rules for degraded contrast cases
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Text replacement can change button width and shift layout. Mitigation: use fixed min-width token for primary to prevent layout jumps
Risk: Icon-only overlay may occlude target hitbox. Mitigation: ensure overlay is pointer-transparent and keyboard focus stays on button
Risk: Backend cannot cancel long-running ops instantly. Mitigation: clearly indicate cancel is a client-side abort attempt and show follow-up status when backend acknowledges
